name: Jezebel and Naboth's vineyard
charge: Judicial murder to seize an inheritance
summary: Ahab coveted Naboth's vineyard; Naboth would not sell his fathers' inheritance. Jezebel arranged false witnesses to accuse him of blaspheming God and the king, had him stoned, and handed the land to Ahab.
offense: Naboth refused to sell or exchange his vineyard because it was the inheritance of his fathers (1 Kings 21:1-3). Ahab's desire for a garden did not extinguish the obligation by which Naboth held the land. The king withdrew in displeasure, and Jezebel promised to obtain what he had been refused. She wrote in Ahab's name, sealed the letters with his seal, and ordered a fast, an accusation by two false witnesses, and Naboth's execution (1 Kings 21:8-14). The elders obeyed. The outward form of judgment was made to serve a conclusion already chosen. Exodus 23:7 forbids slaying the innocent and righteous; the number of witnesses could not cleanse testimony known to be false.
judgment: Ahab went down to take possession, and Elijah met him there with the question joining the crimes: had he killed and also taken possession (1 Kings 21:16-19)? The benefit of the murder stood beside the murder itself. Jezebel's management of the plot did not remove the king's responsibility for receiving its fruit. The Lord pronounced judgment upon Ahab, Jezebel, and their house. Ahab's humbling delayed the destruction of his house, but did not restore Naboth or approve the seizure (1 Kings 21:20-29). Later Joram's body was cast into Naboth's portion, and Jehu recalled the blood of Naboth and his sons (2 Kings 9:25-26). The stolen inheritance remained a witness against the royal house.

verses.text: And it came to pass after these things, that Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard, which was in Jezreel, hard by the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

And Ahab spake unto Naboth, saying, Give me thy vineyard, that I may have it for a garden of herbs, because it is near unto my house: and I will give thee for it a better vineyard than it; or, if it seem good to thee, I will give thee the worth of it in money.
And Naboth said to Ahab, The Lord forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee.

And Ahab came into his house heavy and displeased because of the word which Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him: for he had said, I will not give thee the inheritance of my fathers. And he laid him down upon his bed, and turned away his face, and would eat no bread.
So she wrote letters in Ahab’s name, and sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters unto the elders and to the nobles that were in his city, dwelling with Naboth.
And she wrote in the letters, saying, Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people:
And set two men, sons of Belial, before him, to bear witness against him, saying, Thou didst blaspheme God and the king. And then carry him out, and stone him, that he may die.
And the men of his city, even the elders and the nobles who were the inhabitants in his city, did as Jezebel had sent unto them, and as it was written in the letters which she had sent unto them.
They proclaimed a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people.

And there came in two men, children of Belial, and sat before him: and the men of Belial witnessed against him, even against Naboth, in the presence of the people, saying, Naboth did blaspheme God and the king. Then they carried him forth out of the city, and stoned him with stones, that he died.
And the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, which is in Samaria: behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, whither he is gone down to possess it.

And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Hast thou killed, and also taken possession? And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the Lord, In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.
And of Jezebel also spake the Lord, saying, The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.
And when Jehu was come to Jezreel, Jezebel heard of it; and she painted her face, and tired her head, and looked out at a window.
And as Jehu entered in at the gate, she said, Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?
And he lifted up his face to the window, and said, Who is on my side? who? And there looked out to him two or three eunuchs.
And he said, Throw her down. So they threw her down: and some of her blood was sprinkled on the wall, and on the horses: and he trode her under foot.
And when he was come in, he did eat and drink, and said, Go, see now this cursed woman, and bury her: for she is a king’s daughter.
And they went to bury her: but they found no more of her than the skull, and the feet, and the palms of her hands.

Wherefore they came again, and told him. And he said, This is the word of the Lord, which he spake by his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, In the portion of Jezreel shall dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel:
And the carcase of Jezebel shall be as dung upon the face of the field in the portion of Jezreel; so that they shall not say, This is Jezebel.

entries.commentary: Naboth had a vineyard next to Ahab's palace in Jezreel, and Ahab asked to trade or buy it, offering a better vineyard or its worth in money. Naboth refused because the land was the inheritance of his fathers. He could not simply hand off an inheritance that was given to him. -

Ahab went home heavy and displeased, laid down on his bed, turned away his face, and would eat no bread. He threw a fit and sulked because he could not get his way, angry that a subject would not surrender his inheritance.

Jezebel came to Ahab and asked why his spirit was so sad that he would not eat, and he told her Naboth's refusal. Jezebel mocked his weakness, telling him he was king and should let his heart be merry, and she promised to get the vineyard of Naboth for him.

Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed them with his seal, sending them to the elders and nobles of Naboth's city. The seal was a signet, an official mark of the king's authority, so the letters carried royal weight as if Ahab himself had written them. She commanded them to proclaim a fast, set Naboth on high, and set two sons of Belial before him to bear false witness that he blasphemed God and the king, then stone him. This was evil counsel and a murderous plot. -

The elders and nobles obeyed Jezebel's letters, proclaimed a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people. Two children of Belial, children of the devil, sat before Naboth and falsely witnessed that he had blasphemed God and the king. They carried Naboth out and stoned him to death, then sent word to Jezebel that he was dead.

When Jezebel heard Naboth was dead, she told Ahab to arise and take possession of the vineyard he had been refused. Ahab rose up and went down to take the vineyard. This is extortion, seizing what another has by violence and force. Ahab shares the guilt. He sat by and let Jezebel commit the crime because he coveted the field, then turned his face from the evil and went to claim the reward. -

The word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite to go down and meet Ahab in the vineyard of Naboth. Elijah was to declare, Thus saith the Lord, hast thou killed and also taken possession, and in the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth, dogs would lick Ahab's own blood.

Ahab called Elijah his enemy, and Elijah answered that he had found him because Ahab had sold himself to work evil in the sight of the Lord. The Most High would bring evil on Ahab, cut off every male of his house, and make his house like the house of Jeroboam and the house of Baasha because of the provocation by which he made Israel to sin. The phrase him that pisseth against the wall refers to the males, whom the Most High said he would cut off entirely. -

The Most High declared that the dogs would eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel. Any of Ahab's house dying in the city the dogs would eat, and any dying in the field the fowls of the air would eat, matching the curses spoken in the law. -

There was none like Ahab, who sold himself to work wickedness in the sight of the Lord, stirred up by Jezebel his wife. He did very abominably in following idols, as did the Amorites whom the Most High cast out before the children of Israel.

When Ahab heard these words he rent his clothes, put on sackcloth, fasted, and went softly, humbling himself before the Most High. Because Ahab humbled himself, the Most High told Elijah he would not bring the evil in Ahab's own days but would bring it upon his house in his son's days. The judgment was not cancelled but delayed and transferred to the next generation, showing that genuine humbling before the Most High moves his hand. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement)

Elisha sends one of the children of the prophets to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu king over Israel, pour the oil on his head, and flee. Jehu is charged to smite the house of Ahab to avenge the blood of the prophets and of the servants of the Most High shed at the hand of Jezebel, whose work was to kill the prophets while weak Ahab let it continue. The word declares the whole house of Ahab shall perish, and the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel with none to bury her.

Jehu's fellow captains ask why the mad fellow came, and when he tells them the prophet anointed him king, they hasten to put their garments under him and blow the trumpets, proclaiming Jehu king. Jehu conspires against Jehoram and charges that none escape the city to carry the news to Jezreel. He rides toward Jezreel where Jehoram lay wounded, and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see him.

A watchman spies Jehu's company, and two horsemen sent to ask if it is peace are each told to turn behind him and do not return, for the driving is furious like the driving of Jehu. Jehoram himself goes out and asks if it is peace, and Jehu answers that there can be no peace while the whoredoms and witchcrafts of his mother Jezebel are so many. Jehu draws his bow with full strength and smites Jehoram through the heart, then casts him into the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite according to the word of the Most High.

Ahaziah king of Judah flees but Jehu pursues and has him smitten in his chariot; he flees to Megiddo and dies there. His servants carry him to Jerusalem and bury him in the sepulchre of his fathers in the city of David.

Jezebel paints her face and tires her head, returning to her seductive ways as Jehu enters the gate. Jehu calls out for who is on his side, and two or three eunuchs look out. At Jehu's word they throw her down, her blood is sprinkled on the wall and the horses, and he treads her under foot. When they go to bury her they find only the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands, fulfilling the word spoken by Elijah that dogs would eat the flesh of Jezebel and her carcass would be as dung upon the field.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not covet anything that is your neighbor's.
You shall not bear false witness against another nor raise a false report.
One witness shall not condemn a man for any iniquity or crime he commits.
